region: Burdett · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Osmote is the small winery of Ben Riccardi, who grew up outside Ithaca and studied viticulture and enology at Cornell. He spent seven years chasing harvests in France, New Zealand and Sonoma, then ran the wine program at City Winery in Manhattan before coming home. His first vintage, in 2014, was about 200 cases of Seneca Lake Chardonnay. Today he and his wife, Britt, farm a 31-acre property on the southeast shore of Seneca Lake in Burdett, with an orchard, gardens and pasture-raised pigs alongside the winery.

Riccardi’s Riesling comes from two hillside sites on either side of Sawmill Creek, which tumbles over waterfalls into the east side of Seneca Lake: the steep Sawmill Creek Vineyard, planted in 2005, and the flatter Peach Orchard Vineyard, planted in 2011. The grapes are picked by hand and pressed as whole clusters, then fermented with native yeasts in neutral 400- and 500-liter French oak barrels. The wine rests on its lees until about a month before bottling, a recipe for texture rather than oak flavor.

Osmote makes deliberately light, lower-alcohol wines with bright acidity and minimal added sulfur. Critic Jamie Goode, tasting a recent Osmote Riesling, found citrus, pear and apple fruit with real depth and a rich, juicy texture; expect lime zest, green apple and white peach set against crushed stone. Osmote recommends its Riesling with fried food, fresh seafood or a pungent cheese, or simply as an aperitif.
facts: Sawmill Creek and Peach Orchard, east side of Seneca Lake
Hand harvested, whole-cluster pressed, native-yeast fermentation
Neutral 400–500 L French oak barrels, on the gross lees
